main_text.l: TERTIA PARS
De vero nati Christi tempore.
PRÆFATIO.

l.i: Quare Evangelista annum Herodis aut Augusti in describendo

main_text.l: §. 1 N[?]d[?] notias, quod utrumque Evan-
gelistam Matthæum & Lucam
rei hujus duxisse, modo natalem Chri-
sti cum anno Herodis Regis com-
ponat, caeterum die, mense,
& die nativitatis ejus minus sollicitus
[?]. Vulgatissimus est quarumcunque gentium mos, re-
rum gestarum historias, quas describunt, ad tempora
Regum & Principum revocare, sub quorum imperio
res gestae sunt; non tamen semper ut curent, ut
eorum annos numerare componant. Cum ideo Herodis
natale Christi tempori indefinitè componunt Evangelistae,
forte propter dubium (idest, duplicem) regni
ejus epocham & æram haud utile censebant annum regni
ejus apponere, cum alii numeret annos à decreto
Senatus Romani, alii à nece Antigoni: ut illam
confusionem evitare potius duxerint. Dein notare oportet,
quod Herodis iter hic notaverit uterque Evangelista,
non ad temporis articulum definiendum, sed ad
Messiæ adventus Christi indicandam: quasi dixerint,
nondum derelictus erat Herodes Rex Judæorum, vo-rum

page.notes: The scan is blurred and faded, especially in the first lines under the woodcut initial and in the line "cum divino Herodis Regis", so the first words of §. 1 and some words in the lines beside the initial are doubtful and marked [?]. The last line is partly obscured; the word "rum" is the end of the word hyphenated at the line end. Where I wrote "iter" and some words in the final lines, the reading is a best guess from the blurred letters and should be checked against the original. The heading "TERTIA PARS" is an ordinal word, so caput="3" is my reading of its number. Show-through from the reverse page is not transcribed.
